subject: giraffe
pitch: A young reticulated giraffe. Chestnut patches outlined by bright cream lines all over its body and neck, a short mane of stiff brown hair down the neck, two fuzzy ossicones with black tufts on top, big ears, long lashes, a long dark tongue just peeking out, and slender legs fading to cream above the hooves.
reasoning:
I'm working out realistic proportions for a young giraffe and planning the color palette to use in the model.

Now I'm figuring out how to render the reticulated coat pattern using patch and gradient functions, blending chestnut patches into cream near the hooves for a countershading effect on the legs.

I'm also laying out the skeleton: setting the hips as the root joint, building a spine chain from pelvis to shoulders, and shaping the long neck with a catmull curve that tilts sharply upward and forward, like a real giraffe's posture.

For the head, I'm placing a joint at the neck's tip, oriented forward and slightly up so it reads as an elongated skull with a forward-pointing snout. I'm structuring the neck as a chain of four joints so each segment aims toward the next, with the head attaching to the final neck joint, while the torso gets its own spine chain running from the rump up to the withers along a gentle curved path.

Simplifying further: hips as root, then a spine chain to withers, a neck chain with three joints, and finally the head joint attached to the neck tip with an aim direction pointing forward and slightly upward.

Now I'm working out the leg geometry — placing hip and shoulder joints, then checking whether a two-segment limb chain can actually reach from shoulder down to the ground given giraffe proportions. I'm realizing the reach isn't sufficient with my initial segment lengths, so I need to lengthen the limb segments to match a taller giraffe shoulder height.

Setting torso center around y 1.9-2.0 with barrel bottom at 1.6, shoulder joint at 1.7. For overall height, withers ~2.05 and head/ossicones topping out near 3.0-3.1, roughly matching a young giraffe's proportions, scaled as needed.

For the leg chains, I'm working out the joint naming scheme: four points (shoulder, elbow, wrist, hoof) giving three spans, with the chain parented to the appropriate spine/chest joint.

I'm simplifying the spine setup — rather than creating a redundant hips joint separate from the chain start, I'll make "hips" the root joint directly at the base position, then build the spine chain from there to the withers, with front legs parented to the resulting chest joint.

Now I'm placing the leg attachment points: shoulders forward-high for front legs, hips further back for rear legs, with hoof targets positioned roughly under the chest and body respectively. For the knee/elbow bend directions on each three-segment limb, I'm keeping the front legs bending uniformly forward while alternating the rear legs' bend directions to get a more natural digitigrade stance.

I'm also adding small hoof cylinders at each limb's tip joint, sized and positioned so their bottom face sits at ground level, and planning a subtle cream color gradient along the lower legs for visual fading.

Now I'm working out how to sweep tube geometry along each leg chain, tapering the radius from wider at the top to slender near the hoof, then applying the same sweeping approach to the body's spine with a barrel-like radius profile that bulges in the middle.

For the torso shape, I'm defining an elliptical cross-section that varies in width and height along a curved spine path running from the rump through the chest, using a catmull-rom path to control the overall silhouette and some sinusoidal variation so the body reads as rounded rather than tubular.

I'm sweeping the body along the spine chain with varying radius, then building a separate neck chain path curving upward from the withers with its own tapering sweep radius, accepting a small seam where they join. For the mane I'm thinking of using stiff brown hair cards or spikes along the top of the neck.

Figuring out mane geometry...

Now I'm moving on to the ossicones -- planning them as fuzzy horn-like stubs sprouting from the top of the head, using a rod or capsule shape with a black tuft on top, and working out the head's joint position to anchor them correctly.

Planning the head joint's local coordinate placement for the skull, muzzle, and eyes, using forward/up/left offsets so the giraffe's pale muzzle and dark eye spheres sit correctly relative to the head bone, choosing array-based positions over keyword directions to avoid sign confusion with mirrored sides.

Still working out the eye ring orientation...

Now thinking through the ears — they need to be lateral and leaf-shaped, so I'm working out the plane and normal direction so the ear faces outward to the side (+X for the left ear), using cross products to confirm the outline's x/y axes produce the right facing normal, then mirroring for the right ear.

Writing the ear outline coordinates...

Then I'm moving to the tongue, using a simple capsule shape with tapered radius from the mouth outward for a peeking-out effect, and starting to block out the muzzle as a box positioned ahead of the skull.

For the box orientation, I'm reasoning that geometry defaults to model-space world axes unless explicitly oriented, so the snout box's depth axis should align with the head's forward direction without extra rotation. I'm then working out ossicone placement directly in model coordinates near the top of the head, approximating base and tip positions since the head joint's local "up" doesn't map simply to world Y.

Switching to absolute model-space coordinates for all head features to avoid ambiguity: defining the skull box center and dimensions, then placing eyes on its side faces, ears further back, and ossicones near the top. I'm also laying out the snout box in front of the skull and sketching tongue capsule geometry extending from the mouth opening.

Now I'm setting up patch-based coloring for the body, using cream outlines splitting chestnut patches, and reusing that pattern on the head. I'm also considering whether to add a short tufted tail for visual appeal, starting its path near the hips.

Still writing tail geometry...

Now I'm defining the body's spine radius profile with sinusoidal tapering for a rounded barrel shape, checking that leg attachment points stay within body bounds, and giving the rear end rounded caps.

I'm sweeping the neck chain with tapering radius and matching body color, then adding hooves as cylinder parts attached to leg tip joints, and working out the shoulder and hip joint positions for the four legs relative to the body's z-range.

Now I'm figuring out foot placement under the body, adjusting x/y/z offsets for front versus rear legs, and naming each leg's chain joints with left/right suffixes so they stay unique when mirroring. I'm checking the limb and chain function signatures to confirm how root/target points map to named joints, making sure each leg gets a shoulder, elbow, wrist, and hoof name matching the path's span count.

I'm also sketching the sweep radii for legs so they taper from thicker at the top to slender at the hoof, and cross-checking the hip joint position against the body's cross-section radius at that spine point to make sure the legs emerge naturally from the torso rather than poking through visibly. Then I'm moving on to naming the spine chain joints -- hips, back segments, withers -- to build out the body's joint hierarchy.

Working out the neck chain next, matching path points to joint names, then setting the head joint's position and aim direction so it tilts slightly forward and up from the neck tip, following the neck's natural tangent.

For the mane, I'm distributing small spike geometries along the neck sweep using the `along` helper, orienting each spike outward from the surface frame. For the ossicones I'm using tapered capsules, and for the head tuft I'm clustering a few small spheres with slight positional offsets near the ossicone tips.

For the eyes, I'm placing small spheres on the sides of the head with a sideways-facing direction, then adding a ring of lash spikes along the upper arc of each eye using `b.ring` with angle and tilt parameters. For the ears, I'm reasoning through the orientation needed so the flat leaf shape sticks out sideways and back from the skull rather than facing forward, then defining an extrude outline with points sweeping from the base to a rounded tip, mirrored for left and right sides.

I'm also laying out the snout and skull as boxes with cream and body paint, adding a dark tapered capsule for the tongue peeking out, and setting up the tail as a two-joint chain with a tapering sweep and a small tuft sphere at the end. Then I move into writing the actual build function: importing the builder utilities, defining color constants (chestnut, cream, mane brown, dark, hoof, ossicone, tongue), creating patch and gradient paints for the body and legs, and constructing the skeleton starting from the hips joint through a catmull-rom spine chain, body sweep, neck chain and sweep, head joint with an aim target, and then attaching all the head details (mane spikes, ears, eyes, lashes, ossicones, snout, tongue) and the tail.

Now I'm working through the ossicones -- defining base and tip points for a tapered capsule, then scattering a few small dark spheres around the tip to form the knob, considering sphere resolution and offset placement so the cluster reads as a rounded tip. I move on to a helper function for building each leg: using `limb()` to generate a bent path between a top joint and a foot target with bend direction hints, differentiating front legs (shoulder-elbow-wrist-hoof naming) from rear legs (hip-knee-hock-hoof), then sweeping each leg chain with a gradient paint that shifts from the body's patched color up top to cream near the hoof, and capping each with a cylinder hoof geometry positioned at the ground.

I'm working out specific coordinates for each of the four legs -- front and rear, mirrored left/right -- choosing top and foot positions and segment length ratios so the proportions look right, and deciding which spine or hip joint each leg chain should parent to. I also reconsider the tail's color and the sphere tuft placement, verifying the API signatures I'm using for capsule, part, extrude, and ring calls, and double-checking that eye and lash colors are distinct enough. Satisfied the whole skeleton and surface definition is consistent, I'm ready to write out the final module with the meta export and the complete build function.
